summary: Learn to review system designs, build threat models, and produce secure architecture decisions in a practical 5-day course.
lede: Design-stage security reviews examine system blueprints before implementation to find trust-boundary, identity, and control gaps. For security architects, product security engineers, and others who assess application, cloud, or integration designs, the course develops skills in tracing data flows, drafting STRIDE threat models, and documenting risks with actionable control recommendations.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who review system designs, shape security patterns, and make architecture decisions under delivery pressure. Security Architects responsible for reviewing application trust boundaries and control placement. Product Security Engineers assessing architecture risks before release approval. Application Security Analysts documenting threat models and design review findings. DevSecOps Engineers embedding secure design checks into delivery workflows. Cloud Security Architects reviewing identity, segmentation, and logging patterns. Enterprise Architects aligning security controls with reference architectures. Technical Leads resolving design trade-offs with engineering teams. IAM Specialists validating authentication, authorization, and privilege boundaries. Security GRC Analysts tracking design exceptions and risk acceptance decisions. Infrastructure Architects securing hybrid deployment patterns and service dependencies.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of application security principles, software development lifecycles, and basic cloud or infrastructure concepts. Familiarity with threat modeling, authentication and authorization, and common architecture diagrams is helpful. No programming is required, but you should be comfortable reading system designs, interpreting data flows, and discussing controls with engineers and architects.
